:::{#sol-identity-matrix-shape}

No.
Every [identity matrix](#def-identity-matrix) $\matr{I}_p$ is $p \times p$,
so it is [square](#def-square-matrix).
$\matr{J}$ is $2 \times 3$,
so it is not square.
Therefore $\matr{J}$ is not an identity matrix,
even though its [main diagonal](#def-main-diagonal) holds ones
and its other entries are zeros.

:::
